217:
(a) Licenses which may be issued under this chapter shall be as follows:
(1) Manufacturing:
a. Malt beverages.
b. Wine.
c. Spirituous liquors.
(2) Wholesale:
a. Malt beverages.
b. Wine.
c. Spirituous liquors.
(3) Retail package:
a. Malt beverages.
b. Wine.
c. Spirituous liquors.
d. Sunday sales.
(4) Consumption on the premises:
a. Malt beverages.
b. Wine.
c. Spirituous liquors.
d. Sunday sales.
e. Consumption on the premises establishments (add retail sales of unopened beer or wine from display area for carry-out purposes only), per alcoholic beverage.
f. Growlers (for craft draft beers only, for purchase and consumption off premises) per calendar or any portion of a calendar year.
(5) Retail consumption dealer (on-premises consumption):
a. Malt beverages.
b. Wine.
c. Spiritous liquors.
d. Sunday sales.
1. Provisions for Sunday sales for retail consumption dealer shall be in accordance with subsection 6-20(b)(2) of this chapter.
(6) Wine specialty shop (add on for package license only):
a. Wine.
b. Growlers (for craft beers only).
c. Craft draft beers.
(7) Brewpubs with eating establishments (add on malt beverage consumption on premises only).
An individual procuring one or more of the aforementioned licenses shall pay a fee as fixed by the mayor and board of aldermen as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file with the office of the city clerk.
(b) Any combination of the above at the same location provided no retail or wholesale licensee shall hold any consumption on the premises license for the same location, unless approved by the city manager, or designee.
(c) A person doing business at more than one place shall take out and pay for a separate license for each place of business.
(d) Any new license issued before July 1 shall not be subject to proration. Any new license issued on or after July 1 shall be subject to half the annual license fee without further proration.
(e) If the wholesale dealer's principal place of business is located within the city, the city will levy a license fee in accordance with the classification into which the applicant falls. In addition to the general occupation tax, the wholesale dealer shall pay a fee, as fixed by the mayor and board of aldermen, and as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file with the office of the city clerk, to cover the expenses of investigation and processing. Permit applications of wholesale dealers located within the city shall be approved by the city manager, or designee. If the wholesale dealer delivers alcoholic beverages based on orders previously taken, no license fee shall be required, but the wholesaler shall be required to register with the business license manager, on a form prescribed by the city, prior to delivery of any alcoholic beverages.
(f) Additional requirements for manufacturers, distilleries, breweries, and brewpubs:
(1) No malt beverages, wines, distilled spirits, or any other alcoholic beverage shall be stored, delivered, sold, or manufactured in the city except under a license issued pursuant to this chapter and then only for the specific beverage and manner of sale provided in the license.
(2) The requirements of this chapter shall be in addition to any other requirements for business licenses under this Code and if other provisions of this Code conflict with this chapter then this chapter shall control.
(3) All breweries and distilleries operating under a state manufacturer's license shall be subject to the same restrictions as retailers and retail consumption dealers with the following maximum sales limits as in accordance with state law:
a. Distilleries: 500 barrels annually and 2,250 milliliters per consumer per day for premises consumption.
b. Breweries: 3,000 barrels annually and 288 ounces per consumer per day for off-premises consumption.
c. Brewpubs: 10,000 barrels annually, up to 5,000 barrels of which can be sold to licensed wholesalers.
(4) Licenses may be renewed as provided in O.C.G.A. § 3-3-1 et seq.
(5) Licensed malt beverage manufacturers and licensed distilled spirit manufacturers shall be permitted to sell their respective beverages to the public as permitted by state law, O.C.G.A. 3-5-24.1(b) and O.C.G.A. 3-4-24.2(b), subject to the taxation requirements for consumption and retail, in addition to all other provisions of this chapter.
(6) Seizure of identification. Any brewer or distiller, or any person acting on behalf of such brewer or distiller, who upon requesting proper identification from a person attempting to purchase alcoholic beverages from such brewer or distiller pursuant to state law is tendered a driver's license which indicates that such driver's license is falsified, is not the driver's license of the person presenting it, or that such person is under the age of 21 years, the person to whom said license is tendered shall be authorized to either write down the name, address, and license number or to seize and retain such driver's license and in either event shall immediately thereafter summon a law enforcement officer who shall be authorized to seize the license either at the scene or at such time as the license can be located. The procedures and rules connected with the retention of such license by the officer shall be the same as those provided for the acceptance of a driver's license as bail on arrest for traffic offenses pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 17-6-11.

218:
(a) City alcoholic beverage licenses shall not become effective until each business which is required to obtain an alcohol license from the state has registered with the state and is in good standing with the state or has received such license from the state.
(b) At the time a new applicant submits an alcoholic beverage license application to the city, a copy of the state license application and/or forms shall be required for processing.
(c) New applicants shall be required to submit to the city a copy or proof of the state license for the alcohol license establishment immediately upon receipt of the state license and no later than 45 days after receiving a city license.
(d) Renewal licensees shall be required to submit to the city a copy or proof of the current state license for the alcohol license establishment by January 31 of each year.
(e) The city may issue an alcoholic beverage license to an alcohol license establishment at the time a background check is made, and fees are paid for renewal of such a license. However, a copy and/or proof of the current state license must be submitted annually by the licensee in order for the city alcoholic beverage license to remain in effect. The city shall indicate on the alcoholic beverage license certificate that, "This license is invalid without the state alcohol license, as per Section 6-5 of the City of Acworth, Georgia, Code of Ordinances."
(f) The alcoholic beverage license shall be subject to revocation in the event the applicant does not submit to the city a copy and/or proof of the state license in a timely manner as per section 6-5(c) and (d).
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2009-14, § 1, 10-15-2009; Ord. No. 2009-18, § 2, 11-5-2009; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
219:
(a) All businesses licensed pursuant to this chapter must open for business within 90 days after the issuance of such city license. Failure to open for business within such 90-day period of time shall constitute a forfeiture and cancellation of the issued license, and no refund of the license fees or business taxes shall be made. Any applicant unable to comply with the time limit of this subsection may make written request to the city manager, or designee, for an extension of such time limit, not to exceed 90 days; and the city manager, or designee, at its discretion, may grant or deny such request.
(b) Any license issued under this chapter shall automatically be null and void where the licensed business has not operated or been open to the public for six consecutive months. Any applicant unable to comply with the time limit of this subsection may make written request to the city manager, or designee, for an extension of such time limit, not to exceed 90 days; and the city manager, or designee, at its discretion, may grant or deny such request.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
220:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person within the city, who has any direct financial interest in a license for the sale of alcoholic beverages at wholesale, to hold any other license or an interest in any other license under the terms of this chapter, unless otherwise allowed by state law.
(b) It shall be unlawful for any person related within the first degree of relationship or affinity under civil law to any wholesale licensee or employee of such licensee, or any person with any interest in such licensee, to hold any other license or an interest in any other license issued under this chapter, unless otherwise allowed by state law.
(c) No elected or full-time appointed official of the city, or any person related within the first degree of consanguinity or affinity under civil law to such an official of the city, shall own any interest in any license issued under this chapter, unless one of the following conditions shall be met:
(1) The interest was obtained prior to election or appointment to office;
(2) The interest is declared in writing at the time the application for such license is made, and the elected or full-time appointed official shall not participate in official action or consideration of the license; or
(3) The interest obtained in an ongoing business holding a license is declared in writing at the time of the acquisition and filed with the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
221:
Each application for a malt beverage, wine, or spirituous liquor license, including Sunday sales, whether manufacturing, wholesale, retail package or consumption on the premises, shall include a fee as fixed by the mayor and board of aldermen and as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file with the office of the city clerk. Said fee will cover the expenses of advertising, investigation, and processing of the application. All applications shall be subject to approval by the city manager, or designee.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2019-28, § 1, 10-17-2019; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021; Ord. No. 2022-16, § 1, 6-16-2022)
222:
(a) All new businesses at locations in the City of Acworth (Cobb County) where an alcoholic beverage license has not previously been issued, where there is a change of ownership of the alcoholic beverage license, or where there is any change of licensee and the new licensee has not previously attended a responsible alcohol sales and service policy workshop, applicant/licensee will be required to attend a certified workshop as approved by the city clerk.
The applicant/licensee shall attend said workshop, at their own expense, prior to the issuance of any alcoholic beverage license. The applicant/licensee shall present a certificate of completion of an alcohol sales and service policy workshop prior to the submission of an alcoholic beverage license application, however, if an applicant/licensee has been previously certified by an approved vendor selected by the city clerk, a new certificate shall not be required.
(b) The provisions of this section shall apply to renewal applications. Under no circumstances shall the workshop provision be waived. It shall be the responsibility for all certified applicants/licensees to train their employees including, but not limited to, alcohol servers and managers.
(c) Effective July 1, 2021, for all new alcoholic beverages license applications and/or renewals, the applicant/licensee must provide a copy of written policy or procedures for training their employees including, but not limited to, alcohol servers and managers. Written policy or procedures must ensure that all alcoholic beverage sales are carried out in a fashion that complies with city ordinance and/or state law to include, but not limited to, the number of servings allowed for patrons and that no sales are made to the underage or minors.
(d) In the event of revocation or suspension of an alcoholic beverage license, instructors, trainers, or any persons associated with or employed by approved certification vendors shall not appear before the city manager, or designee, or board of aldermen as a representative, attorney, advocate, or witness for any applicant/licensee.
(Ord. No. 2014-26, § 1, 11-20-2014; Ord. No. 2019-04, § 3, 2-7-2019; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
223:
(a) All applicants for licenses under this chapter shall be bona fide residents of the United States at the time of the filing of the application and shall remain a bona fide resident during all times that the license, and any renewal of such license, is in effect. All applicants, if a natural person, all managers designated as such, and all registered agents nominated pursuant to this section shall be at least 21 years of age.
(b) All applications for licenses under this chapter shall nominate and name in the application one or more residents of the State of Georgia as the registered agent and representative of the applicant to receive all communications, notices, services or process or other papers or documents on behalf of the applicant in connection with any matter arising out of or connected with the issuance, holding, suspension, revocation, or other action with respect to any city license. The applicant for a license shall give the mailing address of such registered agent, and the mailing to any registered agent at such address of any notice required to be given under this chapter or any other law shall be deemed as sufficient notice to the applicant/licensee.
(c) The registered agent shall be a representative of the licensee, and must be approved by the city manager, or designee. The city manager, or designee, shall refuse to approve any registered agent who is not a bona fide resident of the United States and a resident of the State of Georgia, or who has been convicted, within the five years preceding his nomination, of any felony of any kind, any misdemeanor relating to an alcoholic beverage business or any state law or county or municipal ordinance violation relating to any alcoholic beverage business.
(d) If any registered agent shall cease to be a representative of the licensee, shall cease to be a resident of the United States and the State of Georgia, or in any manner ceases to meet the requirements of subsection (c) of this section, the licensee shall notify the city clerk in writing of such event, and shall nominate a new registered agent within three days after such event occurs. Such new registered agent shall meet the requirements of subsection (b) and (c) of this section, and must be approved by the city manager, or designee. The city shall charge a fee, as fixed by the mayor and board of aldermen, and as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file with the office of the city clerk, for a change of the licensee's registered agent; provided, however, that if the licensee fails to notify the city and nominate a new registered agent within such three-day period, then the city may charge an alterative fixed fee for a change of the licensee's registered agent and/or to revoke the licensee's license.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2005-22, 5-5-2005; Ord. No. 2015-06, § 1, 5-7-2015; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021; Ord. No. 2022-16, § 1, 6-16-2022)
224:
(a) The city manager, or designee, shall cause an inquiry to be made into the city tax records to determine if an applicant for a license under this chapter, or other parties with interest in such application, has any outstanding taxes or special assessments that are delinquent against his property or any other moneys owing to the city. No license under this chapter shall be issued or renewed until such debts are paid in full.
(b) All applications for licenses under this chapter shall be reviewed by the chief of police or his designee as a condition to action on and issuance of a license by the city manager, or designee. If the police department determines that the application is not in order, in view of the requirements of federal or state law or this Code and any police department investigation, the city manager, or designee, shall then notify the applicant of the reasons for not issuing the license to the applicant.
(c) All applicants for licenses under this chapter shall furnish all reasonable data, information and records requested of such applicants by the city, and failure to furnish such data, information, contracts, documents, financial statements, and other records within 30 days of the request for such material shall automatically serve to dismiss the license application.
(d) The police department may require, in addition to the licensee, fingerprinting and a background investigation of any person interested in the license application, including any person with a financial interest, such as stockholders, partners or employees, and any sibling of any person with a financial interest, and the nominated registered agent of any corporate applicant. Should the applicant fail to produce such persons within 30 days of the request, the police department shall recommend denial of the application.
(e) By filing an application for a license under this chapter, the applicant agrees to produce for interview any person requested by the police department and considered as being important in the ascertainment of the facts relative to such license. The failure to produce such persons within 30 days after being requested to do so may result in a denial of the application by the police department.
(f) The city may require 45 days for processing any application for a license under this chapter. For investigative purposes and according to the licensee's compliance, the chief of police may extend the processing period up to an additional 15 days if the police chief shall deem such extension necessary.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
225:
An applicant for a license under this chapter shall cause to be placed upon the location of the premises proposed to be licensed, signs of a size, number and form prescribed by the city manager, or designee, stating the names of the owners of such premises, and the address of the applicant, type of license applied for, business name and location applied for, and the time, date and location of the city manager, or designee, meeting on the application. such signs shall be posted at the location within a two-week period immediately preceding the meeting date of the city manager, or designee, meeting.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
226:
Any business taxable under this chapter which moves from one location in the city to another shall notify the office of the city clerk in writing of the move and the new address on a form provided by the business license department. Such business shall be considered a new applicant and shall be subject to the requirements of section 6-8.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000)
227:
of ownership.
(a) The transfer of ownership of an alcoholic beverage license shall be considered in the same manner as the termination of the business and the establishment of a new business. If the owner of an alcoholic beverage license desires to transfer such license, or if any interest in the business for which the license was issued is sold or otherwise transferred, the purchaser or transferee of such license or interest shall apply to the city as for an original license on or before the date on which such sale or transfer is made. Ownership of such alcoholic beverage license shall remain unchanged until the application of such purchaser or transferee is approved by the board of aldermen and all proper fees and taxes are paid. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in the case of a corporation, a new license shall not be required as provided in this section, unless a change in stock ownership in the corporation results in ownership of more than 50 percent of the outstanding corporate stock, voting or otherwise, by persons or a combination of persons who are not owners of such stock at the time the original license was issued. The term "any interest" means being an ownership of stock or control of 50 percent or more of the partnership or corporation.
(b) The transfer of ownership of a business licensed under this chapter shall not affect the distance requirements previously approved by the city.
(c) Upon the sale or other transfer of any interest in the business for which a license was issued under this chapter, the purchaser or transferee of such interest shall be entitled to continue to operate such business for a period of no more than 60 days, pending the issuance of a new license, but only if such purchaser or transferee has filed an application with the city as required in subsection (a) of this section. In case of the death of any natural person holding a city business license, or any interest in such license, the license may be transferred to the administrator, executor of the lawful heir or devisee of the deceased person by filing a new application with the city for the change in license ownership within 75 days of such death. The business involved may continue to operate until disposition of the application is determined as for an original license. No additional fees or business taxes shall be charged above what would be due if the business, or portion thereof, remained under the deceased person's ownership.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2019-28, §1, 10-17-2019; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
228:
If a building in which any person intends to operate under the provisions of this chapter is, at the time of the application for a license under this chapter, not in existence or not yet completed, a license may be issued for the location, provided, the plans for the proposed building clearly show a compliance with the other provisions of this chapter. No sales or consumption of alcoholic beverages shall be allowed in the establishment until it has been completed in accordance with the plans and is in conformity with all of the other provisions of this chapter and this Code.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
229:
(a) A license under this chapter shall not be issued, renewed or transferred to any person, partnership or corporation where any individual having any interest, either as owner, partner or stockholder, directly or indirectly, beneficial or absolute, shall have been convicted of any felony within five years immediately prior to the filing of the application, or convicted of any misdemeanor relating to any alcoholic beverage business or any municipal ordinance violation relating to any alcoholic beverage business within two years immediately prior to the filing of the application. The term "any interest" means an ownership of stock or control of 50 percent or more of a partnership or corporation.
(b) The term "conviction" shall include an adjudication of guilt, a plea of guilty or nolo contendere, or the forfeiture of a bond, in part or in whole, when charged with a crime, or the suspension or revocation of any alcoholic beverage license owned, in whole or in part, by persons listed in subsection (a) of this section.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
231:
All licenses issued under this chapter shall be subject to the rules and regulations set forth in an act of the general assembly known as the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Laws and Regulations, 1986 edition, to legalize and control alcoholic beverages and liquors, as amended, and the rules and regulations prescribed by the state department of revenue. Violation of such statutes and regulations shall be a violation of this chapter. In addition, all businesses, the applicant for a license under this chapter, the agent in charge of the licensed business and the owners of such business, shall observe and obey the regulations provided in this article, and any other applicable provisions of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2021-15, § 1, 6-17-2021)
232:
Any establishment holding a license issued under this chapter shall, at all times during the hours that the establishment is open to the public, be open to inspection by any officer of the police department, any license inspector of the city or any person designated by the chief of police, or the city manager or his designee.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000)
233:
(a) No bottle or other containers of alcoholic beverages shall be opened or consumed by any person on the premises upon which the place of business is conducted and licensed under this chapter, whether the bottle or container so opened or consumed was bought or obtained at the place of business or elsewhere, unless the premises is licensed under this chapter for consumption on the premises, except in the case of those places of business which are licensed for a wine specialty shop. These businesses may also allow sampling of wines or craft draft beers so long as there is no charge for admittance for the wine sample or craft draft beer sample and the serving size does not exceed one and a half ounces.
(b) An establishment licensed under this chapter to sell alcoholic beverages shall not allow any person to leave such licensed premises with any alcoholic beverage in an open cup, bottle, can or other open container.
(c) This section shall not apply to city-sanctioned events. A city-sanctioned event is an event which is approved by a vote of the mayor and board of aldermen, or an event for which a permit is granted to any department, agency, board or commission of the city, and the city downtown development authority.
(Ord. No. 2000-3, 3-2-2000; Ord. No. 2004-22, § 1, 6-3-2004; Ord. No. 2011-22, § 1, 9-1-2011; Ord. No. 2013-11, § 3, 4-18-2013; Ord. No. 2020-15, § 1, 7-16-2020)
234:
The purpose of this section is intended to set forth certain exceptions and provisions applicable only to licensees whose establishments:
(1) Are located within the open container district.
(2) Possess a license to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises.
Except as specifically set forth in this section, all such licensees will remain subject to all other provisions of the city's alcoholic beverages ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2014-19, § 1, 7-3-2014; Ord. No. 2020-15, § 1, 7-16-2020)
235:
The mayor and board of alderman shall adopt through a resolution a map with boundaries of the open container district.
(Ord. No. 2014-19, § 1, 7-3-2014; Ord. No. 2020-15, § 1, 7-16-2020)
236:
(a) Container. No container in which an alcoholic beverage is dispensed and removed from the licensed premises shall exceed 16 fluid ounces in size. No person shall hold in possession on the public streets and sidewalks, plazas, in parks and/or any other public place within the defined area any open alcoholic beverage container which exceeds 16 fluid ounces in size. Any establishment licensed to sell alcoholic beverages by the drink for consumption on the premises is authorized to dispense an alcoholic beverage in a clear plastic cup for removal from the premises.
(b) Drinking from can, bottle, or glass prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any person to drink or attempt to drink any alcoholic beverage from an un/open can, bottle, glass, or plastic cup (other than clear) or to possess in an open can, bottle, or glass on the public streets, sidewalks, plazas, rights-of-way, and parking lots, whether public or private.
(c) Purchase from licensed premises within the district. Alcoholic beverages consumed pursuant to this provision must be purchased from a licensed premise within the historic downtown district.
(d) Consumption limited to certain areas in district. No alcoholic beverage purchased pursuant to this provision may be consumed outside the district or upon any private property without the consent of the property owner.
(e) Regulated hours. The hours of operation for the containment area shall begin pursuant to section 6-20 and shall end at midnight. It is prohibited to be in the district with any alcoholic beverage outside of these hours.
(Ord. No. 2014-19, § 1, 7-3-2014; Ord. No. 2020-15, § 1, 7-16-2020)
237:
Any establishment that allows patrons to leave an establishment with an alcoholic beverage as regulated herein shall have an 11-inch by 17-inch sign posted at the door for public view whereas a patron exiting the establishment can read the following:
"All patrons leaving this establishment with an alcoholic beverage do hereby take full responsibility to only consume an alcoholic beverage in the immediate open container district and any individual that leaves the permitted area with an alcoholic beverage is in violation of City Code and may be subject to a citation and/or fine."
(Ord. No. 2014-19, § 1, 7-3-2014; Ord. No. 2020-15, § 1, 7-16-2020)
238:
The provisions of this article shall not be deemed to abrogate or otherwise impact any state law or local ordinance pertaining to public drunkenness, disorderly conduct, driving with an open container or under the influence of alcohol, or similar laws.
(Ord. No. 2014-19, § 1, 7-3-2014)
239:
As set forth in O.C.G.A. § 3-6-4, notwithstanding any other contrary provision of law, any restaurant which is licensed to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises may permit a patron to remove one unsealed bottle of wine per patron for consumption off premises, if the patron has purchased a meal and consumed a portion of the bottle of wine which has been purchased on the premises with such meal on the restaurant's premises. A partially consumed bottle of wine that is to be removed from the premises must be securely resealed by the licensee or its employees before removal from the premises. The partially consumed bottle of wine shall be placed in a bag or other container that is secured in such a manner that it is visibly apparent if the container has been subsequently opened or tampered with, and a dated receipt for the bottle of wine and meal shall be provided by the licensee and attached to the container. If transported in a motor vehicle, the container with the resealed bottle of wine shall be placed in a locked glove compartment, a locked trunk, or the area behind the last upright seat of a motor vehicle that is not equipped with a trunk.
(Ord. No. 2014-24, § 1, 10-16-2014)
240:
(a) Spirituous liquor package sales. It shall be unlawful for any licensee under this chapter or person employed by a licensee to sell, offer for sale, transfer or offer to transfer to other persons packaged spirituous liquors between the hours of
12:00 a.m.—8:00 a.m. on Monday
1:00 a.m.—8:00 a.m. on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday
12:00 a.m.—11:00 a.m. on Sunday
And it shall be unlawful for any person to purchase, receive or offer to receive from a licensee or person employed by a licensee any packaged spirituous liquors during the hours listed in this section.
(b) Sales by consumption on-premises licensees. It shall be unlawful for any licensee under this chapter or person employed by a licensee to sell, offer for sale, transfer or offer to transfer to any other person any spirituous liquors, malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises between the hours of 2:55 a.m. on Sunday and 8:00 a.m. on the following Monday morning, and between the hours of 2:55 a.m. and 8:00 a.m. on all other days of the week; and it shall be unlawful for any person to purchase, receive or offer to receive from a licensee or person employed by a licensee any spirituous liquors, malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises between the hours of 2:55 a.m. on Sunday and 8:00 a.m. on the following Monday morning, and between the hours of 2:55 a.m. and 8:00 a.m. on all other days of the week, provided, establishments licensed for consumption on the premises which derive at least 50 percent of its total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sale of prepared meals or food in all of the combined retail outlets of the individual establishment where food is served and in any licensed establishment which derives at least 50 percent of its total annual gross income from the rental of rooms for overnight lodging shall be permitted to sell spirituous liquors and/or malt beverages on Sundays between the hours of 11:00 a.m. and midnight upon approval and issuance of a permit authorizing such sales. License applications shall be submitted to the city manager who shall issue such licenses upon payment of a fee as established from time to time by the mayor and board of aldermen to establishments meeting the applicable requirements of this chapter and/or state law. In the case of restaurants, the alcoholic beverage Sunday sales license application and the required fees may be submitted at the same time as all other license applications. The city shall have 90 days to determine if the application qualifies for Sunday sales of alcoholic beverages. During such 90-day period, the applicant shall be granted a temporary permit which shall automatically expire 90 days after issuance. If the applicant qualifies for Sunday sales of alcoholic beverages, then the applicant shall be issued an annual Sunday sales permit. If the applicant qualifies for Sunday sales of alcoholic beverages, no further fees shall be necessary. If the applicant does not qualify for Sunday sales of alcoholic beverages, the city will retain all fees paid under this subsection, including the processing fee, as fixed by the mayor and board of aldermen and set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file with the office of the city clerk.

283:
(a) The mayor and the board of aldermen finds as follows:
(1) According to numerous public health research studies, alcohol remains the number one drug of choice among young people in the United States.
(2) "The Surgeon General's Call to Action To Prevent and Reduce Underage Drinking," which can be found at http://www.surgeongeneral.gov/topics/underagedrinking/calltoaction.pdf., cites a comprehensive body of facts that demonstrate the risks to communities from underage drinking; they include the following:
a. "Early alcohol consumption by some young people will result in an alcohol use disorder—that is, they will meet diagnostic criteria for either alcohol abuse or dependence." (page 4)
b. "While adolescents typically drink alcoholic beverages less often than adults, when they do drink alcoholic beverages, adolescents tend to drink more alcoholic beverages at each event than adults." (pages 6—7)
c. "Annually, about 5,000 people under age 21 die from alcohol-related injuries involving underage drinking." (page 10)
d. "Underage drinking "can cause alterations in the structure and function of the developing brain, which continues to mature into the mid—to late twenties and may have consequences reaching far beyond adolescence." (page 11)
e. "Underage drinking "can cause a range of physical consequences, from hangovers to death from alcohol poisoning." (page 11)
The Surgeon General's Report also identifies alcohol as a contributing factor in many activities that place others as well as the underage alcohol user at risk. These activities include physical and sexual assault, risky sexual behavior, loud and unruly behavior, property damage, unintentional injuries, violence, and even death. For example, "about 45 percent of people who die in car crashes involving a drinking driver under the age of 21 are people other than the driver." (page 11)
(b) Moreover, the mayor and the board of aldermen finds as follows:
(1) Persons who are less than the age of 21 often possess or consume alcoholic beverages at social parties or gatherings held at or on private residences and other private property under control of a person who either has provided the alcoholic beverages or who knows or reasonably should know of such conduct, but fails to take steps to prevent it.
(2) Law enforcement agency responses to disturbances involving underage consumption of alcoholic beverages at parties or gatherings at or on private residences or other private property frequently require the use of extensive public resources.
(3) Further, when law enforcement personnel respond to such disturbances it limits their ability to respond to other service calls in the community, thereby placing the community at increased risk. Law enforcement is not currently reimbursed for their expenses when called to a party or gathering at or on a private residence or other private property.
(c) As such, the mayor and the board of aldermen declare as follows:
(1) Protecting health and safety in the city is a reasonable cause to deter the possession and consumption of alcoholic beverages by persons under the age of 21. It is also reasonable and prudent to do by holding responsible persons who encourage, are aware of, or should be aware of, the illegal conduct, yet fail to take steps to prevent it.
(2) Further, there is data to demonstrate that public efforts to deter the possession and consumption of alcoholic beverages by persons under the age of 21 will result in significant costs savings with regard to law enforcement (citation and prosecution), healthcare (i.e., emergency room treatment)) and rehabilitation (addiction and recovery). As such, the revenue received by the city, after cost reimbursement to responding law enforcement agencies, will be directed toward law enforcement strategies and prevention programs in the city.
(Ord. No. 2014-23, § 1, 10-2-2014)

(12) Such other identification and information as the police department may require in order to discover the truth of the matters specified in this section as required to be set forth in the application.
(13) The age and date of birth of the applicant, of any partners, or of any and all officers, of any stockholders of more than five percent of the shares of the corporation stock outstanding, directors of the applicant if the applicant is a corporation.
(14) If the applicant, any partners or any of the officers or stockholders holding more than five percent of the outstanding shares of the corporation, or the directors of the applicant if the applicant is a corporation have ever been convicted of any crime constituting a felony, or any crime not a felony involving moral turpitude, in the past five years, and, if so, a complete description of any such crime, including date of violation, date of conviction, jurisdiction and any disposition, including any fine or sentence imposed and whether terms of disposition have been fully completed.
(15) The fingerprints of the individual applicant.
(16) If the applicant is a person doing business under a trade name, a copy of the trade name properly recorded. If the applicant is a corporation, a copy of authority to do business in the state, including articles of incorporation, trade name affidavit, if any, and last annual report, if any.
(17) At least three character references from individuals who are in no way related to the applicant or individual shareholders, officers or directors of a corporation and who are not or will not benefit financially in any way from the application if the license is granted and who have not been convicted of any felony or crime involving moral turpitude in the past five years. The city manager shall prepare forms consistent with the provisions of this subsection for the applicant, who shall submit all character references on such forms.
(18) Address of the premises to be licensed.
(19) Whether the premises are owned or rented and, if the applicant has a right to legal possession of the premises, copies of those documents giving such legal right.
(20) A plat by a registered engineer, licensed by the state, showing the location of the proposed premises in relation to the neighborhood, the surrounding zoning, and its proximity to any church, school, public park, governmental building or site or other business regulated under this article.
(b) Each applicant for an adult entertainment establishment permit shall be verified and acknowledged under oath to be true and correct by:
(1) The individual, if the applicant is an individual.
(2) The manager or general partner, if a partnership.
(3) By the president of the corporation, if a corporation.
(4) By the chief administrative official, if any other organization or association.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 12, 10-7-1993)
314:
The applicant for a permit under this division, if an individual, or designated responsible managing officer, if a partnership or corporation, shall personally appear at the city and produce proof that a nonrefundable application fee, as fixed by the mayor and board of aldermen and as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file with the office of the city clerk, has been paid and shall present the application containing the required information.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 13, 10-7-1993; Ord. No. 2022-16, § 1, 6-16-2022)
315:
The city shall have 30 days to investigate the application and the background of the applicant for a permit under this division. Upon completion of the investigation, the mayor and board of aldermen may grant the permit if it finds that:
(1) The required fee has been paid.
(2) The application conforms in all respects to the provisions of this article.
(3) The applicant has not knowingly made a material misrepresentation in the application.
(4) The applicant has fully cooperated in the investigation of his application.
(5) The applicant, if an individual, or any of the stockholders of the corporation, any officers or directors, if the applicant is a corporation, or any of the partners, including limited partners, if the applicant is a partnership, has not been convicted in a court of competent jurisdiction of an offense involving conduct or convicted of an attempt to commit any of the offenses referred to in this division, convicted in any state of any offense that, if committed or attempted in this state, would have been punishable as one or more of the offenses, or any crime involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or moral turpitude.
(6) The applicant has not had an adult entertainment establishment permit or other similar license or permit denied or revoked for cause by this city or any other city located in or out of this state prior to the date of application.
(7) The building, structure, equipment or location of such business as proposed by the applicant would comply with all applicable laws, including but not limited to health, zoning, distance, fire and safety requirements and standards.
(8) The applicant is at least 18 years of age.
(9) The applicant, his employees, agents, partners, directors, officers, stockholders or managers, has not, within five years of the date of the application, knowingly allowed or permitted any specified sexual activities to be committed or allowed in or upon the premises where such adult entertainment establishment is to be located or to be used as a place in which solicitations for the specified sexual activities openly occur.
(10) On the date the business for which a permit is required commences, and thereafter, there will be a responsible person on the premises to act as manager at all times during which the business is open.
(11) The proposed premises is not to be located too close to any church, school, library, governmental building or site or any other business restricted under this article.
(12) The grant of such permit will not cause a violation of this article or any other ordinance or regulation of the city, the state or the United States.
(13) Any other inquiry is deemed necessary or desirable by the city to ensure the health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the city or the preservation of its neighborhoods.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 14, 10-7-1993)
316:
No permit provided for by this article shall be issued to or held by:
(1) An applicant who has not paid all required fees and taxes for a business at that location or property taxes.
(2) Any person who is not of good moral character.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 15, 10-7-1993)
317:
No adult entertainment establishment permit may be sold, transferred or assigned by a permittee, or by operation of law, to any other person. Any such sale, transfer or assignment or attempted sale, transfer or assignment shall be deemed to constitute a voluntary surrender of such permit, and such permit shall thereafter be null and void; however, if the permittee is a partnership and one or more of the partners should die, one or more of the surviving partners may acquire, by purchase or otherwise, the interest of the deceased partner without effecting a surrender or termination of such permit; and in such case the permit, upon notification of the city, shall be placed in the name of the surviving partner. An adult entertainment establishment permit issued to a corporation shall be deemed terminated and void when either any outstanding stock of the corporation is sold, transferred or assigned after the issuance of a permit or any stock authorized but not issued at the time of the granting of a permit is thereafter issued and sold, transferred or assigned.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 16, 10-7-1993)
318:
(a) No adult entertainment establishment shall move from the location specified on its permit until a change of location fee, as fixed by the mayor and board of aldermen and as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file with the office of the city clerk, has been deposited with the city and approval has been obtained from the city manager. Such approval shall not be given unless all requirements and regulations as contained in this Code have been met.
(b) No permittee shall operate, conduct, manage, engage in or carry on an adult entertainment establishment under any name other than his name and the name of the business as specified on his permit.
(c) Any application for an extension or expansion of a building or other place of business where an adult entertainment establishment is located shall require inspection and shall comply with the provisions and regulations of this article.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 17, 10-7-1993; Ord. No. 2022-16, § 1, 6-16-2022)
319:
(a) A permittee under this article shall, within ten days after he has been notified of an adverse determination, submit a notice of appeal to the city clerk.
(b) The notice of appeal shall be addressed to the board of aldermen and shall specify the subject matter of the appeal, the date of any original and amended application or requests, the date of the adverse decision (or receipt of notice), the basis of the appeal, the action required of the board of aldermen, and the name and address of the applicant.
(c) The clerk shall place the appeal on the agenda of the next regular meeting of the board of aldermen occurring not less than five nor more than 30 days after receipt of the application for board action.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 18, 10-7-1993)
320:
When an appeal under this division is placed on the board agenda, the board of aldermen may take either of the following actions:
(1) Set a hearing date and instruct the city clerk to give such notice of hearing as may be required by law; or
(2) Appoint a hearing officer and fix the time and place for hearing. The hearing officer may or may not be a city employee and may be appointed for an extended period of time. The clerk shall assume responsibility for such publication of notice of the hearing as may be required by law. If a hearing officer is appointed, the hearing shall be conducted in accordance with the procedures set out in this article.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 19, 10-7-1993)
321:
Whenever the city clerk has scheduled an appeal under this division before the board of aldermen, at the time and date set, the board of aldermen shall receive all relevant testimony and evidence from the permittee, from interested parties and from city staff. The board of aldermen may sustain, overrule or modify the action complained of. The action of the board of aldermen shall be final.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 20, 10-7-1993)
322:
The hearing officer appointed pursuant to the procedure set out in this division may receive and rule on admissibility of evidence, hear testimony under oath, and call witnesses as he may deem advisable with respect to the conduct of the hearing.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 21, 10-7-1993)
323:
The board of aldermen and the hearing officer shall not be bound by the traditional rules of evidence in hearings conducted under this division. Rules of evidence as applied in an administrative hearing shall apply.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 22, 10-7-1993)
324:
(a) The hearing officer shall, within a reasonable time not to exceed 30 days from the date a hearing under this division is terminated, submit a written report to the board of aldermen. Such report shall contain a brief summary of the evidence considered and state findings, conclusions and recommendations. All such reports shall be filed with the city clerk and shall be considered public records. A copy of such report shall be forwarded by certified mail to the permittee/appellant the same day it is filed with the city clerk, with additional copies furnished to the city manager and chief of police.
(b) The city clerk shall place the hearing officer's report on the agenda of the next regular board of aldermen meeting occurring not less than ten days after the report is filed and shall notify the permittee/appellant of the date of such meeting at least ten days prior to the meeting unless the permittee/appellant stipulates to a shorter notice period.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 23, 10-7-1993)
325:
The board of aldermen may adopt or reject the hearing officer's decision in its entirety or may modify the proposed recommendation. If the board of aldermen does not adopt the hearing officer's recommendation, it may:
(1) Refer the matter to the same or other hearing officer for a completely new hearing or for the taking of additional evidence on specific points. In either of such cases, the hearing officer shall proceed as provided in this article.
(2) Decide the case upon a review of the entire record before the hearing officer, with or without taking additional evidence.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 24, 10-7-1993)
328:
Employees of an adult entertainment establishment shall be not less than 18 years of age. Every employee must be of good moral character. Any employee who is convicted of a crime constituting a felony or a crime not a felony involving moral turpitude while employed as an adult entertainment establishment employee shall not thereafter work on any such premises for a period of five years from the date of such conviction unless a longer time is ordered by a court of competent jurisdiction. The term "convicted" shall include an adjudication of guilt or a plea of guilty or nolo contendere or the forfeiture of a bond when charged with a crime, and the terms "employed on such premises" and "work on any such premises" shall include, as well, work done or services performed while in the scope of employment elsewhere than on the premises.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 10(a), 10-7-1993)
329:
Before any person may work on premises regulated under this article, he shall file a notice with the city manager of his intended employment on forms supplied by the city manager and shall receive approval of such employment from the city manager. The prospective employee shall supply such information as the city manager requires, including a set of fingerprints, on regular city or United States Department of Justice forms. Upon approval, the employee may begin working on the premises. If approval is denied, the prospective employee may, within ten days of the denial, apply to the city manager for a hearing. The decision of the city manager after hearing may be appealed to the board of aldermen, which may issue such order as is proper in the premises. An investigation fee, as fixed by the mayor and board of aldermen and as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file with the office of the city clerk, shall accompany the notice of intended employment or a receipt of the city manager evidencing the payment of such fee at the time the notice is filed.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 10(b), 10-7-1993; Ord. No. 2022-16, § 1, 6-16-2022)
330:
Violation of the provisions of this Code, the ordinances of the city, laws and regulations of the state, or the rules and regulations of the city shall subject an employee to suspension or revocation of his permit.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 10(c), 10-7-1993)
331:
For the purpose of this article, independent contractors shall be considered as employees and shall obtain a permit as employees, regardless of the business relationship with the owner or permittee of any adult entertainment establishment.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 10(d), 10-7-1993)
334:
(a) No person shall advertise or cause to be advertised an erotic dance establishment without a valid adult entertainment establishment permit issued pursuant to this article.
(b) No later than March 1 of each year, an erotic dance establishment permittee shall file a verified report with the city manager showing the permittee's gross receipts and amounts paid to dancers for the preceding calendar year.
(c) An erotic dance establishment shall maintain and retain for a period of two years the names, addresses and ages of all persons employed as dancers.
(d) No adult entertainment establishment permittee shall employ or contract with as a dancer a person under the age of 18 years or a person not licensed pursuant to this section.
(e) No person under the age of 18 years shall be admitted to an adult entertainment establishment.
(f) An erotic dance establishment may be open only between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m. Monday—Friday, and Saturday from 8:00 a.m.—2:55 a.m. on Sunday. No permittee shall permit his place of business to be open on Christmas Day.
(g) No erotic dance establishment shall serve, sell, distribute or suffer the consumption or possession of any intoxicating liquor or controlled substance upon the premises of the permittee.
(h) An adult entertainment establishment permittee shall conspicuously display all permits required by this section.
(i) No dancing shall occur closer than ten feet to any patron.
(j) No dancer shall fondle or caress any patron, and no patron shall fondle or caress any dancer.
(k) No patron shall directly pay or give any gratuity to any dancer.
(l) No dancer shall solicit any pay or gratuity from any patron.
(m) All areas of an establishment licensed under this section shall be fully lighted at all times patrons are present. Full lighting shall mean illumination equal to 3.5 footcandles per square foot.
(Ord. No. 93-023, § 3(a)—(m), 10-7-1993)
336:
Footnote 3:
State Law reference— Gambling, O.C.G.A. § 16-12-20 et seq.; state licensing of coin-operated amusement machines, O.C.G.A. § 48-17-1 et seq.
338:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Amusement center means any establishment operated for profit that houses more than six mechanical or electronic amusement devices within one enclosure.
Coin-operated amusement machine means any amusement machine operated by means of the insertion of a coin, token or similar object, for the purpose of amusement or skill and for the playing of which a fee is charged. The term "coin-operated amusement machine" does not include vending machines which do not incorporate gaming or amusement features, nor does the term "coin-operated amusement machine" include any coin-operated mechanical musical machine.
Operator means any person who sets up for operation by another, or leases or distributes for the purpose of operation by another, any coin-operated amusement machine, whether such setting up for operation, leasing or distribution is for a fixed charge or rental, or on the basis of a division of the income derived from such machine, or otherwise.
Proprietor means any person who, as the owner, lessee or proprietor, has under his control any establishment, place or premises in or at which a coin-operated amusement machine is placed or kept for use or play, or on exhibition for the purpose of use or play.
(Code 1983, § 11-51)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
339:
Any person violating any of the provisions of this article, in addition to the revocation of his license, shall be guilty of an offense.
(Code 1983, § 11-52)
340:
Each operator or licensee under this article shall, at all times, open every portion of the licensed premises for inspection by the police department and other city departments for the purpose of enforcing any provisions of this article.
(Code 1983, § 11-56(a))
341:
Each operator or licensee shall have present on the premises or on such portion of the premises where the coin-operated amusement machine is located, as the case may be, at least one adult operator at all times the premises are open to the public, who has not been convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude and who has been so certified by the police department.
(Code 1983, § 11-56(b))
342:
A licensee under this division shall, at all times, control the sound so as not to cause disturbance or nuisance to others in the vicinity of the machines. The licensee shall, at all times, place the machine so that the part of the machine from which the sound emits shall not be within five feet of the front entrance of the place of business; and the licensee shall not, at any time, place a music machine so that the sound is disturbing to the public in the street or to other persons occupying the building in the immediate vicinity.
(Code 1983, § 11-56(c))
343:
No operator or licensee under this article, by himself, directly or indirectly or by any servant, agent or employee shall permit:
(1) Any indecent, immoral or profane language, or indecent, immoral or disorderly conduct.
(2) The licensed premises to become a resort for disorderly persons of any type.
(3) Gambling or the use, possession or presence of gambling paraphernalia in the premises. The winning of anything of value as a result of the operation of a machine shall constitute gambling.
(4) Intoxicated persons to loiter on the premises.
(5) The possession or use of any unlawful drug or narcotic, including marijuana, on the premises.
(6) Noise or music to emerge from the licensed premises.
(7) Unless accompanied by an adult 21 years of age or older, any person under the age of 17 years to operate or play any machine or device during the hours of 7:30 a.m.—3:30 p.m. on such days as any school within the school district where the premises are located is open for regular school attendance.
(Code 1983, § 11-56(d))
344:
Nothing in this article shall in any way be construed to authorize, license or permit any gambling devices whatsoever, or any mechanism which has been judicially determined to be a gambling device or in any way contrary to law or that may be contrary to any future law of the state. Any operator or proprietor or other firm, partnership or corporation that shall permit in any way, directly or indirectly, gaming or gambling in the use of any device or machine shall be subject to immediate confiscation of such device or machine by the police department as contraband, and shall be punishable as a misdemeanor, unless other punishment is authorized under the laws of the state.
(Code 1983, § 11-58)
345:
Nothing contained in this article shall in any way be construed to authorize, license or permit any machine or device which exhibits or allows the viewing of photographs or moving pictures of an obscene or pornographic nature, or in any manner prohibited by law or the ordinances of the city. Any operator or proprietor or other person who shall permit in any way, either directly or indirectly, any such use of any device or machine shall be subject to immediate confiscation of such device or machine by the police department as contraband and shall be punishable as a misdemeanor, unless otherwise provided by law.
(Code 1983, § 11-59)
348:
No person shall engage in the business of an operator or proprietor of coin-operated amusement machines without first having obtained the proper license, after payment of the proper fee provided for in this article and having complied with the other provisions of this article.
(Code 1983, § 11-53(a))
349:
An application for amusement center licenses shall be made to the city clerk with the payment of the prescribed annual license fees. The application must be signed and sworn to by the applicant in the case of a sole proprietorship. If the applicant is a partnership, all partners must sign and verify the application. If the applicant is a corporation, any authorized officer and the secretary must sign and verify the application and indicate their official positions. The information required in the application form must be furnished as to each person signing the application. Each application shall be accompanied by the required licensing fee and shall contain the following information:
(1) The applicant's full name.
(2) The applicant's residence address.
(3) The applicant's business address.
(4) The address of the proposed amusement center.
(5) The name and address of every person who has any interest in the amusement center, and the nature of that interest.
(6) Whether or not the applicant has been convicted of a felony.
(7) Whether or not the applicant, at the time of making the application, is keeping or in any way connected with a gaming house or a house of ill fame.
(8) Whether or not the applicant, the applicant's spouse or any member of the applicant's household is a member or employee of the police department of the city; whether or not any member or employee of the police department of the city is interested in any way, either directly or indirectly, in the license applied for, the devices or their operation; and whether or not the applicant has received or borrowed money or anything else of value or accepted credit from any member or employee of the police department or the spouse or any member of the household of any member or employee of the police department.
(9) A statement that the applicant permits a record of his fingerprints to be made by the police department of the city for the purpose of additional investigation to determine whether or not the application should be granted.
(10) Written approval of the chief of police or his authorized representative, who shall issue such approval when he finds that the applicant is not guilty of any of the violations or facts listed in subsection (6), (7) or (8) of this section.
Upon receipt of the proper application and the fee and approval, the city clerk may then issue a license for the center. No license shall be valid except for the location shown in the application. Any false or misleading statement contained on the application shall be grounds for revocation.
(Code 1983, § 11-53(b); Ord. No. 2004-11, § 1, 3-18-2004)
350:
Before any license under this article shall be issued, an investigation of the applicant and an inspection of the premises shall be made by the building inspector, county fire marshal, police department and such other city departments or agencies as may be deemed necessary to determine whether the applicant, the devices or machines and the premises fully comply with all pertinent ordinances and regulations. For standards for such determination the following shall be considered:
(1) No license shall be issued where the location of the premises or any device or machine located on the premises shall constitute a nuisance or danger so as to impede safe ingress or egress from the premises.
(2) All wiring and connections to each machine or device shall comply with the electrical code and fire code of the city.
(3) No machine or device shall be placed or located so as to constitute a nuisance through sound, or otherwise, to others. The placement and control by licensee of each machine shall, at all times, not be such that the sound is disturbing to the public in the street or in any other portion of the building.
(4) Minimum off-street parking facilities provided shall comply with the zoning ordinance or shall be not less than one space per two devices or machines, whichever is the greater requirement; and the premises shall be located so as not to impede the normal flow of traffic.
(5) No license shall be granted except in a C-1, C-3 or PSC zoning district, or where all city codes are not being complied with.
(6) No license shall be granted to any applicant who makes any false or misleading statement in the application; or who is not of good moral character; or who has been convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude or for the sale or use of any drug, alcohol or other intoxicant, or any other violation of the laws of the state or the ordinances of the city that may tend to corrupt the moral integrity of any other person.
(7) No license shall be granted to any applicant at any location unless every provision of this article is complied with and completed, and later noncompliance shall be grounds for revocation of the license.
(8) No license shall be granted for any location which is within 500 feet of any public school giving instruction at least five days a week, holidays excepted, for eight or more months per year, or any church or house of worship of any religious faith, or nursing home, rest home or public library.
(9) No license shall be granted for any location unless the building inspector and the chief of police shall have determined that the lighting outside the proposed location is adequate to deter accidents to vehicles and pedestrians and to deter illegal or illicit activity within a distance of 50 feet of the premises.
(Code 1983, § 11-53(c))
351:
Any license required under this division shall be purely a personal privilege and shall not constitute property. It is not transferable in any manner.
(Code 1983, § 11-53(d))
352:
Each licensee under this division shall display an approved license provided by the city. Not more than one location shall be operated under one license, except as otherwise provided. The revocation of any license granted under this division shall operate to revoke all licenses issued to any licensee or any location granted or approved under this division. In addition, the operator, proprietor or amusement center shall at all times display in a conspicuous place the appropriate license granted the licensee in a location near the entrance to the establishment where such machine is located.
(Code 1983, § 11-53(e))
353:
(a) All licenses under this division must be renewed annually, at which time the board of aldermen may request reverification of all requirements under this article for the purpose of determining whether the applicant has conformed to the rules and regulations of this article in determining whether such license shall be renewed.
(b) The license fees shall be as fixed by the mayor and board of aldermen as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file with the office of the city clerk.
(c) All fees shall be payable annually in advance. Where application for licensee, location or machine is made after January 10 of any license year, a license may be issued, at the discretion of the board of aldermen, for the remainder of the year, upon payment of a proportionate part of the annual fee, prorated to the nearest quarter of a year. In no case shall any part of the license fee be refunded to the licensee.
(Code 1983, § 11-54; Ord. No. 2022-16, § 1, 6-16-2022)
354:
The right to revoke every license issued under this division is expressly reserved should the location, the licensee or the operation of any coin-operated amusement machine be contrary to any provision of this article. The licensee shall be given five days' notice at the licensed location of the time, date and place of the hearing to show cause why such license should not be revoked, together with the violations of the article or law charged, and may appear, with or without counsel, and submit evidence in his defense.
(Code 1983, § 11-55)
355:
Except as hereafter provided, upon the decision of the chief of police or his/her designee to approve or deny a license under this chapter, such decision being in writing and including notice of the decision and notice of the appeal procedures to the mayor and board of aldermen as provided hereafter, the applicant or any aggrieved citizen may appeal the decision of the chief of police to the mayor and board of aldermen by filing a written notice of appeal with the city clerk within five calendar days of the decision by the chief of police or his/her designee. Every appeal shall be in writing and identify the basis for such appeal and upon receipt of the appeal; the city clerk shall forward same to the board of aldermen which shall schedule a hearing within 45 days of receipt of such notice. The board of aldermen may sustain or overrule the decision of the city clerk. The action of the mayor and board of aldermen shall be final and may be appealed to superior court in accordance with state law.
(Ord. No. 2004-10, § 1, 3-18-2004)
358:
A licensee under this article who operates an amusement center shall provide the following:
(1) A minimum of one on-site, off-street parking space for each amusement machine or device requested.
(2) A uniformed security guard or at least one full-time supervisory person who shall be on the premises at all times during the hours of operation.
(Code 1983, § 11-57(1), (2))
359:
No person under the age of 17 years shall be permitted in amusement centers during the hours of 7:30 a.m.—3:30 p.m. on such days as any school within the school district where the premises are located is open for regular school attendance unless accompanied by an adult 21 years of age or older.
(Code 1983, § 11-57(3))
360:
(a) During the months of September—May of each year, amusement center operators shall only operate during the hours of 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m., Monday—Thursday, and during the hours of 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 midnight, Friday and Saturday, and from 1:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. on Sunday.
(b) During the months of June, July and August of each year, amusement center operators shall only operate during the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 12:00 midnight Monday—Saturday, and from 1:00 p.m. to 12:00 midnight on Sunday. The license shall not be valid for operation during any other hours.
(Code 1983, § 11-57(4))
361:
(a) No amusement center nor any coin-operated amusement device in an amusement center shall be operated so as to constitute a public nuisance.
(b) It shall be the responsibility of the licensee to maintain order on the licensed premises at all times.
(c) It shall be the responsibility of the licensee to see that the licensed premises do not become overcrowded so as to constitute a hazard to the health or safety of persons in the center.
(Code 1983, § 11-57(5)—(7))
362:
It shall be unlawful for any person engaged in the business of operating an amusement center to sell, offer for sale or knowingly permit to be sold or offered for sale or to be dispensed or consumed or brought onto the licensed premises, any alcoholic beverages.
(Code 1983, § 11-57(8))
363:
Every amusement center licensed under this division shall have affixed on its premises, in plain view, evidence of the issuance of its license.
(Code 1983, § 11-57(9))
364:
The license required and described in this division shall be purely a personal privilege and shall not constitute property. It is not transferable in any manner.
(Code 1983, § 11-57(10))
365:
Any violation of the Criminal Code of Georgia (O.C.G.A. tit. 16), or of any ordinance, pertaining to obscene materials as defined in such code, shall result in immediate revocation of a license issued under this division.
(Code 1983, § 11-57(11))
368:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Busker means a person who performs in a public place for donations.
Busking means performing in a public place for donations.
Perform means but is not limited to, the following activities: acting, singing, playing musical instruments, pantomime, juggling, magic, dancing, reading, puppetry, and reciting. Perform shall not include the production of items for sale.
Performer means a person who has obtained a permit pursuant to this section.
